role: Places an entity arriving through a portal: finds the nearest nether portal block within 128 blocks (cached per arrival column), builds a new portal when none exists, and for the End builds the 5x5 obsidian platform. Stale cache entries are dropped every 100 ticks.
scope_reason: Nether and End travel are vanilla and in scope (SPEC Decisions: the Nether and the End are vanilla worldgen; dimension travel is in the loop).

members.name: random
members.note: struct teleporter.rand, seeded new Random(world.getSeed()) in teleporter_init.

members.name: destinationCoordinateKeys
members.note: portal_cache.keys keeps insertion order for the stale sweep.

members.name: placeInPortal
members.note: Includes the End branch: the 5x5 obsidian platform and air above. Non-player travellers reach it through serverreplay.c's sr_travel_place.

members.name: removeStalePortalLocations
members.note: Called from WorldServer.tick's tail in serverreplay.c.

notes: GPU hazard for the native port (belongs to the portal.c record): the portal cache is heap allocated and grows (malloc/realloc) instead of a fixed-capacity array. The placement search itself is bounded (257x257 columns x actual height). Exact status is from the nether-trip and end-arrival recordings named in DEVLOG; I did not run them. Since lane/endreturn (2026-09-27): end-return-s42 re-enters the End after a death and a respawn, and the arrival platform is rebuilt over a broken obsidian cell and a placed cobblestone row.
